title: Every Window
logline: When the lighthouse goes dark, an old keeper wakes a whole village to become its light.
look: Paper theatre on rods and pins, lamp-lit from below; storm blues and slate, warm amber windows that multiply until the frame glows.
narrator: male, elderly, low pitch, british accent
An old sailor by the fire, slow and weathered, proud at the end
music: Low strings and timpani storm, a lone fiddle for the keeper; each lit window adds a voice until a full warm chorus of strings.

shots.direction: EWS 24mm · slow push · iris in — a paper sea on rods, a lighthouse on a cliff sweeping its beam
MS 50mm · locked · cut — the old keeper winds the lamp; his paper cat watches
CU 85mm · hold · smash cut to dark — the lamp sputters and dies
EWS 24mm · pendulum sway · cut — far out, a small paper ship with one lantern pitches in the storm
MS 35mm · tracking down · cut on action — the keeper hurries down the spiral stairs, lantern in hand
WS 35mm · locked · cut — the sleeping village of paper houses, every window dark; he knocks
CU 85mm · hold · cut — one window lights: a girl with a candle
WS 35mm · slow truck right · cut — windows light one by one down the street; villagers step out with lanterns
WS 24mm · crane up · dissolve — a line of lanterns snakes up the cliff path
MS 50mm · push in · cut — at the top they raise their lanterns behind the great lens; it gathers them into one beam
EWS 24mm · beam sweep · cut — the beam crosses the sea; the ship turns away from the rocks
CU 85mm · hold · cut — the ship's captain lifts her lantern and waves back
EWS 24mm · slow pull back · iris out — dawn on the paper sea; every window in the village still lit

narration.text: On the edge of the world stood one light.
And one night, it went out.
One old man cannot be a lighthouse.
A lighthouse was never one flame. It was everyone who kept it.
